iteration: v139 — decode hot-path pre-allocated buffer benchmark, Qwen3-8B on 2xP150a
optimization_tested: Pre-allocated padding buffers in _pad_decode_batch_fast (v138 commit 6c094a169). Replaces per-step torch.zeros + torch.cat with in-place copy_ into pre-allocated buffers.

decode_timing_ms.samples: 19 batches of 50 steps each (950 steps total)
decode_timing_ms.note: First 50-step batch includes trace capture overhead (+3ms)

comparison.note: Delta is within measurement noise. Pre-allocated buffers eliminated the pad allocation overhead (now 0.00ms vs ~0.01ms before), but that overhead was already negligible. The 36.35ms forward time is the same as v116's 36ms.

buffer_init_log.note: With max-running-requests=1 and data_parallel=1, required_bsz=1 means no padding is needed at all. The fast path exits immediately at actual_bsz == required_bsz.

output_quality.chat_completion: degenerate (BFP8 + Qwen3 chat template, known issue)
output_quality.note: Quality matches v116 baseline. BFP8 artifacts are model-level, not optimization-related.

conclusions: Pre-allocated buffer optimization works correctly: pad phase = 0.00ms (was ~0.01ms with torch.cat)
But SGLang overhead is only 0.1% of total decode time — the optimization target was already negligible
99.9% of decode time is tt-metal decode_forward (36.35ms/step)
With max-running-requests=1 and required_bsz=1, the padding path is actually a no-op (actual_bsz == required_bsz early exit)
The optimization would matter more with batch>1 where actual padding occurs (pad_n > 0)
End-to-end throughput (27.0 tok/s) matches v116 baseline (27.4 tok/s) within noise
The 5.6 tok/s gap to TT vLLM (32.6) is entirely in the tt-metal kernel layer, not SGLang overhead
Timing instrumentation (SGLANG_TT_DECODE_TIMING=1) adds zero measurable overhead (all measurements use perf_counter)
next_steps: The pre-allocated buffer optimization is a no-op for B=1 workloads but is correct infrastructure for future B>1 support
To close the gap to TT vLLM (32.6 tok/s), need tt-metal kernel optimization (DRAM prefetcher or similar)
The timing instrumentation is valuable for ongoing performance monitoring
